# Compose Sampling Oracle

`compose-sampling.tsv` is generated by executing the actual Compose
`SamplingTemplate` and `SimpleperfRecordCommand`, not a second Java implementation.
`SamplingOracle.java` is only the driver and filters the real command into
event/rate/callgraph arguments. Target, transport, duration limits and permissions
are intentionally not claimed equivalent by this fixture.

The 46 cases cover five templates for app/non-app scope, plus two events, three
scopes, frequency/period and three callgraph modes. Template duration is included.
`provenance.json` records the current oracle Kotlin sources and driver hashes.

Regenerate after compiling the Compose capture module:

```sh
cd desktop-viewer
./gradlew -p simpleperf-viewer :capture-simpleperf:classes --offline
cd ..
# CLASSES is capture-simpleperf/build/classes/kotlin/main; STDLIB is the
# kotlin-stdlib JAR for the version pinned in desktop-viewer/gradle/libs.versions.toml.
javac -cp "$CLASSES:$STDLIB" -d "$OUT" rust-desktop/crates/aps-capture/tests/fixtures/SamplingOracle.java
java -cp "$OUT:$CLASSES:$STDLIB" SamplingOracle > rust-desktop/crates/aps-capture/tests/fixtures/compose-sampling.tsv
```

The Rust regression consumes the committed fixture without Java/Gradle at test
time. A fixture update needs fresh Compose execution evidence and source hashes.

`DurationOracle.java` similarly generates `compose-duration.tsv`: seven cases
cover omitted manual duration, whole/fractional seconds and nanosecond notation.
The driver invokes the real Kotlin command builder and normalizes scientific and
decimal forms using BigDecimal. It does not reproduce the builder in Java.
`duration-provenance.json` records its source/driver hashes. Rust retains its
finite, nanosecond-precision, 300-second timed limit; arbitrary upper bounds and
invalid/infinite input are not claimed equivalent to Compose.
